concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The Torah opens with 'לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא לִי אֱלֹקִים' (Psalm 51:12). The concept טהרת הלב appears as the subject and endpoint of multiple eitza edges (cause: שמתלהב ובוער לבו → effect: נטהר הלב). The text does NOT use 'בחינת' for the heart itself in relation to ruach hakodesh in a symmetric/parallel way — instead it says 'when there is purity of heart, ONE THEN MERITS to speak new words which are a bechina of Ruach HaKodesh.' This is cause-and-effect (eitza), not parallel nature (bechina). טהרת הלב is not a bechina of Ruach HaKodesh; it is the precondition that produces it. Therefore excluded from packages.

The Torah's central mechanism is that hitlahavut (fervent burning toward God) purifies the heart. This concept appears only in eitza edges: תנועה → חמימות, חמימות → טהרת הלב, חמימות → גירוש רוח הטמאה. The text never says 'חמימות הוא בחינת X' in a parallel-nature way. Excluded as eitza-only.

Appears in eitza edge 3140: התלהבות וחמימות is achieved VIA תנועה. The teaching describes a physical/intellectual movement that generates warmth. No bechina language equates תנועה to any parallel concept. Excluded.

analysis_notes.note_on_eitza_heavy_torah: Torah #156 is structurally dominated by its causal chain. The Rebbe constructs a tight pathway: תנועה → חמימות → טהרת הלב → גירוש רוח הטמאה → דבורים חדשים = רוח הקדש. Every link in this chain is eitza. The bechina layer is reduced to two paired identity statements: (1) private speech to God IS Ruach HaKodesh, (2) the spirit of impurity IS the spirit of folly. These two pairs constitute the Torah's ontological anchors — the beginning (what holy speech IS) and the obstacle (what the defiling spirit IS) — while the entire middle of the Torah is how-to causality.
analysis_notes.note_on_bracketed_section: Lines 8-13 of the source text are enclosed in parentheses with an editorial note by Reb Noson (line 13) that 'this section was not written properly in order, because I did not hear this matter from his holy mouth himself, but from another in his name.' This caveat does not affect the bechina identification in line 14 (which is NOT bracketed), but does reduce the weight assigned to the physical analogies about arrows and wax (line 8) as primary theological statements.
